Four-week follow-up with neurology consultation; EEG and MRI reviewed and lamotrigine started
Two-month review: lamotrigine at maintenance dose, rash and mood check, and gambling treatment progress
Four-month review of seizure control, mood, and gambling recovery
Eight-month review after a breakthrough seizure and a gambling lapse while traveling
Same-day sick visit for vomiting and diarrhea with missed lamotrigine doses

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Neurology consultation for seizure classification, EEG and MRI review, and the choice of antiseizure medicine
Antiseizure medicine: lamotrigine with slow titration, rash teaching, 30-day supplies, a pill organizer and phone alarms, a seizure diary, and levels only when they would change care

Seizure safety at every visit: triggers (sleep loss, alcohol, overwork), showers rather than baths, no swimming or heights alone, no driving until seizure-free and cleared by his neurologist, a written seizure action plan for friends, and a SUDEP discussion
Gambling-disorder treatment: cognitive behavioral therapy with a gambling-disorder therapist, self-exclusion, a bank gambling block, Gamblers Anonymous, and free debt counseling
Mood and safety: PHQ-9 at intake and every two to four months, GAD-7 at intake and with any change, and a suicide-risk review with the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at every visit
Bone health: baseline vitamin D; lamotrigine is not an enzyme inducer, so no DXA scan is needed unless an enzyme-inducing medicine is added
Reach the lamotrigine maintenance dose without rash by the two-month visit
Maintenance dose of 100 mg twice daily reached after six weeks; no rash
No seizures for six months after reaching the maintenance dose
Not met: one generalized tonic-clonic seizure about five months after reaching the maintenance dose, after missed doses and a night without sleep; the six-month count restarts
Casino and online self-exclusion and a bank gambling block in place by the four-week visit
Self-exclusion from casinos in the state and from licensed online sites, and a gambling block on his bank cards, in place
No gambling through the eight-month visit
Not met: no gambling for about seven months, then a lapse while traveling abroad, outside the reach of his self-exclusion; treatment intensified
Written seizure action plan, safety counseling, and a SUDEP discussion completed by the four-week visit
Plan written and shared with two friends; SUDEP discussed with the neurologist

list.item: Independent in all activities of daily living; after a seizure he is confused and exhausted for several hours and has trouble remembering for a day or two [S]
Alert, articulate, and intense; thought process organized; insight into the harm from gambling; no psychosis [S]
Mood worried; PHQ-9 8 and GAD-7 7; no thoughts of suicide or self-harm [S]

text.paragraph: Structured synthetic safety assessment on 1865-02-03: current ideation absent, intent absent, plan absent. Routine outpatient care. Gambling disorder carries a raised suicide risk, especially after large losses, so safety is reviewed at every visit. He saved the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline and the National Problem Gambling Helpline in his phone and agreed to call either after a large loss or if hopeless thoughts appear. Antiseizure medicine is dispensed as a 30-day supply [S]
